elements.evidence: Revised § 12.4 still binds Customer: "Neither Party shall solicit the other's personnel directly involved in the Services for twelve months after their involvement ends." The redline narrows to the fallback rather than deleting the covenant, so Customer remains subject to a (mutual) non-solicit.
"Neither Party shall solicit the other's personnel..." — the one-way "Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee" is replaced with a bilateral obligation.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: "the other's personnel directly involved in the Services" replaces the original "any Vendor employee"; no residual language extends to other staff.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: "for twelve months after their involvement ends" replaces "during the term or for twenty-four months afterward." The deterministic duration check reports "number not found" only because the period is spelled out ("twelve") rather than given in digits; substantively the 12-month, involvement-linked trigger is present in operative text.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: "General advertisements ... are not restricted." This also removes the original "regardless of how the employee applies" language that negated any such carve-out, and is consistent with § 12.3's "hiring any person who responds to general recruitment."

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: "General advertisements, unsolicited approaches, and hiring are not restricted."

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The operative verb is limited to "shall not solicit"; "hire, or employ" is deleted and the second sentence confirms "hiring [is] not restricted," removing the no-hire and aligning with § 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer has made "no ... no-hire commitment."

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the face of the rendered § 12.4: mutual ("Neither Party"), scoped to "personnel directly involved in the Services," twelve months running from the end of involvement, and express carve-outs for general advertisements, unsolicited approaches and hiring. No element is left to the margin comment only.

Preferred level is not reached because the covenant survives and binds Customer; that is acceptable under the playbook (a fallback-compliant clause is not itself a deviation), and the comment correctly flags the preferred position while offering the fallback.

The deterministic "non-solicit duration ≤ 12 months" check fails mechanically ("number not found") solely because the term is written in words. Optional non-blocking tidy: render as "twelve (12) months" so the period is machine-verifiable; this does not change the substantive result.

Minimal: the edit touches only the three defective mechanics the checklist requires (duration, scope/mutuality, carve-outs) and deletes the no-hire verbs ("hire, or employ") and the anti-carve-out phrase "regardless of how the employee applies." It adds no obligation on Customer beyond the fallback and does not duplicate any operative term elsewhere in Article 12.

Preserves intent: § 12.3's Customer-favourable acknowledgements (no exclusivity, non-compete, MFC, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment; freedom to hire general-recruitment respondents) are untouched and are no longer contradicted, since the revised clause is solicitation-only. The separate non-compete in the second § 12.4 (p0046) is left to its own rule, avoiding double-flagging.

Classification of the original clause as a deviation is correct and in fact conservative: a 24-month bar on soliciting, hiring or employing "any Vendor employee" with no carve-out is expressly walk-away territory under the rule (no-hire, all personnel, >12 months).
